props.covers: The per-group gesture contracts: bare placement payloads and the folded shape vocabulary, the geometry gestures and their text-fit warnings, the kind-agnostic content gestures, section framing and the lock matrix, the six edge gestures with the fresh-polyline contract, the delete cascades, and the perception, annotation, and run-ending calls.

Restyling a wire, repointing it, and cleaning up its route are separate motions on the real canvas, so they are separate calls here.

replaces the interior corners wholesale; the two ends stay attached where they are.

— consecutive corners share an x or a y, including the two legs that join the endpoints. Validation asks the router rather than a rulebook: it snaps the points, checks the consecutive-pair rule for a precise message, then routes a candidate edge and rejects anything the router would have quietly fallen back on. A rejection names where the router attaches each end, so the corrected call is computable from the error. A silently ignored route would be worse than a refusal: the edge would keep auto-routing while the model believed it had placed the wire.
is the fine instrument: it slides one segment perpendicular to itself, the way dragging its handle does.

is the segment's new x when it is vertical and its new y when it is horizontal, so orthogonality is preserved by construction. It drives the canvas package's own bend machinery with a synthetic drag, which is why a model-driven shift and a pointer-driven one land the same document patch, endpoint re-pins included. An index the edge does not have is refused with the available segments listed, and a near-diagonal run — which has no bend handle on stage either — is refused with a redirect to
. Both refusals print the current route.

moves one end to another object, or to another side of the one it already meets; the edge alone moves and neither object changes. When the ends move it drops a stored manual route explicitly, with a note, because waypoints drawn for the old geometry describe nothing afterwards. Distinctness is judged against the edge as it will stand — the side being repointed against the side already stored — so a repoint cannot land on the object the other end occupies.

is the close-up. It changes nothing and frames exactly
names a section or a single object — a section frames its own bounds, an object frames its bounds with a ring of context around them — and

measured — per-pair gaps on each axis, row and column pitch, the section's free margins, ink share — so conformance is read rather than computed in context. The standing text payload rides along with every call: the digest, the cumulative baseline-to-draft diff, every open finding, how every edge actually routes, and the request queue.

The two knobs are either/or, not composable. A call carrying both is refused and told to drop the one that is not the close-up it meant; a bare call with neither is refused and shown what each knob frames. props.title: look never renders the whole board

text.insert: The current board always arrives with the

block, so there is nothing for a whole-board look to add and the tool does not offer one. That is what makes the one-region rule affordable rather than restrictive. The render cadence that keeps the attached board current is the kernel's, and is described in

anchors a question to one object as a thread the user answers on their own time. It never waits: leave the question, proceed on the best reading, and name any open thread in the finalize message. Use it only where the answer would genuinely change the diagram — one or two per run at most.
posts into an existing thread without moving its status, addressed by the thread's queue alias or its annotation id.
is the closing move: it disposes one open queue entry as done or declined, and the note is required — one line for the operator saying what was done, or why it was declined.
replaces the board's standing account wholesale — the full replacement markdown, not a patch.
renames the board: the name shown above it, short, and what a person would call it. The pair goes together when the diagram's subject has moved on from the name it was created with.
is the only call that ends the run, and a successful one is terminal.
proposes the current draft for operator review; it is blocked — and the run continues — while

diagnostic remains in the edited scope, warnings included, while any user-authored request is still open, or while the draft does not differ from the board. The findings it runs are the finishing roster in
). A thread the agent opened is non-blocking, so an unanswered question never traps the run.
ends without a proposal and leaves the board untouched.
is required for both outcomes: one plain-language line, a summary of what changed or the reason no proposal could be made.

props.title: Finalize does not require a prior look

text.insert: should require that the run framed at least one close-up first is an open question. It is unenforced: the gates check findings, open requests, and whether the draft differs from the board, and none of them asks whether the agent ever looked. A run can therefore commit on the board renders attached to its
blocks alone, without a single measured region. Treat the absence of that gate as a decision not yet taken rather than as a decision against it.
